Opp. Party
 Mr.D. Biswal, Asc
 Coram:

Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.
2. This is an application for bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. filed by the Petitioner in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s.498-A/294/323/506 IPC read with Section 4 of the D.P.
Act which was subsequently turned to Sections 376(2)(n)/294/323/506/34 IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act and Section 9 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act in connection with Nimakhandi P.S. Case No.183 of 2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No.03 of 2024 pending in the court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge under POCSO Act, Berhampur.
3.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner and the victim have undergone married and living together as husband and wife.

// 2 //
4. Having regard to the allegations in the F.I.R., there appears ample of material attributed against the Petitioner with regard to the offence under the POCSO Act and as such it is not desirable for this Court to grant anticipatory bail.

However, it is directed that in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned court below, the learned court in seisin over the matter shall dispose of the bail application on its own merit being alive of the position of law on bail keeping in view the gravity of the offences taking into consideration the materials on record as well as other Manoj Kumar Behera @ Tingiri vs State Of Odisha ....
